probe: Bound the repository-native object-retrieval candidate to a falsifiable durability/integrity scope by auditing official Git/GitHub reachability and size limits and cross-checking one current own-role checkpoint through both path-based and blob-OID retrieval surfaces.

observations: Git gc is designed to retain objects referenced by repository refs/history while unreachable objects are eligible for pruning.
The documented default prune expiry for unreachable loose objects is two weeks unless configuration changes it; therefore unreachable-object permanence is not a safe assumption.
GitHub documents an enforced single Git object size limit of 100 MB and recommends substantially smaller objects.
Git read operations are subject to operational throttling guidance, so transport must remain resumable rather than assuming unlimited reads.

reasoning: The same current own-role checkpoint is addressable by its repository path and by its immutable Git blob identity, and both surfaces agree on blob SHA a04da6edb89f69eae3222dc5fe63f911cb607bbd in the tested repository scope.

Official Git garbage-collection documentation makes unreachable-object permanence unsafe: objects that cease to be referenced may be pruned after an expiry window. The candidate therefore must be bounded to objects that remain reachable from repository history/refs rather than treating the object database as an archival key-value store.

GitHub's enforced 100 MB single-object limit is a hard size bound for this repository-native path; rate/throttling limits are operational transport bounds and must be handled by cross-invocation checkpoint/resume.

For already-present reachable state, retrieval consumes no new hosted-storage admission and no finite monthly/trial/paid compute allowance in the tested path. This does not establish that adding arbitrary future payloads is hosted-storage-quota-independent, so whole-root acceptance remains fail-closed.
tested_scope: Official Git gc reachability/pruning documentation and current GitHub repository object-limit documentation, plus one live read-only identity consistency test of reachable own-role checkpoint blob a04da6edb89f69eae3222dc5fe63f911cb607bbd through repository path and Git-database blob-OID surfaces. No object creation, deletion, ref mutation, unreachable-object aging/pruning experiment, rate-limit exhaustion experiment, >100 MB object test, SHA-256 repository test, external storage, hosted compute, protected authority, manual user action, or O/downstream/other-worker semantic input.
scope_negative: No claim of permanent retention for unreachable objects, no claim that GitHub exposes unlimited reads, no claim that new arbitrary payload writes are hosted-storage-quota-free, no claim above 100 MB, no claim for SHA-256 repositories, and no claim of whole-root richer-mode parity.
